quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You are in a minor collision at an intersection. No one is injured and there is little damage. What should you do?

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if you can do so safely.
Do not move your vehicle for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: After a collision with no injuries, move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: This sign warns you that:

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road will get narrower.
There are many curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are many curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to upcoming conditions. This sign warns drivers that the road ahead has many curves.

questions.question: When you see a person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is completely away from your path.
Honk your horn as you drive past them.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is completely away from your path.
questions.explanation: You must stop for pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog. Always give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?

options.text: A tunnel
An intersection
A bridge

questions.correctAnswerText: A bridge
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before the rest of the road and thaw out later. Be careful on bridges in cold weather.

questions.question: To avoid losing traction on wet roads, you should:

options.text: Make sharp turns.
Brake hard.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Lower your speed on wet roads and keep your tires in good condition to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: A broken white line on the highway means:

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross the line to change lanes from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: Oncoming vehicles are to your left and parked vehicles are to your right. Where should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
Halfway between the oncoming and parked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Halfway between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
questions.explanation: Steer a middle path between the oncoming cars and the parked cars.

questions.question: The center line has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line. If the broken line is next to your lane, you can:

options.text: Not pass other vehicles in this area.
Pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
Only make right turns in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
questions.explanation: When a broken yellow line is on your side of the road, you may pass if it is safe and no oncoming traffic is present.

questions.question: You should not enter an intersection if you cannot completely cross before the light turns red:

options.text: In any situation.
Unless you entered on a yellow light.
Unless you entered on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: In any situation.
questions.explanation: Never enter an intersection if you cannot get completely across before the light turns red, even if the light is green. Blocking an intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: Large trucks are most likely to lose speed when:

options.text: Driving up long or steep hills.
Driving through long, gradual curves.
Driving down long, gradual hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks slow down when driving up long or steep hills. Give trucks extra space, especially on hills.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your driving ability?

options.text: Three
Two
One

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even one drink will affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: To see objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, you should check:

options.text: Only the left outside mirror.
Over your left or right shoulder.
Only the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over the correct shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When used on roadways, bicycles are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles when used on roadways. Cyclists and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, use:

options.text: Low beams.
High beams.
Fog lights only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, and snow. High beams will bounce off moisture and create glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must travel through the intersection at the posted speed limit.
The maximum speed limit under ideal conditions is 55 mph.
You must not travel below the speed indicated.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed limit under ideal conditions is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum speed limit for the road. You can drive slower based on conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: Use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days:

options.text: To keep your engine warm.
So others can see your vehicle.
To warn others of bad weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: So others can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: On rainy, snowy, or foggy days, other drivers have trouble seeing your vehicle. Headlights make your car easier to spot. If you need windshield wipers, you must also use low beam headlights.

questions.question: When should your wheels not point straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
questions.explanation: When waiting to turn left, keep wheels straight. This prevents you from being pushed into oncoming traffic if hit from behind. On a hill, turn wheels so your car will not roll into traffic if brakes fail.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: Blind spots disappear if you have one outside mirror.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can check blind spots by looking in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Even with proper mirrors, all vehicles have blind spots. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than regular cars.

questions.question: You should not use your horn:

options.text: When visibility ahead is limited.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near blind pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Using your horn near a blind pedestrian may be dangerous. Yield to the pedestrian and drive when it is safe.

questions.question: Which of the following blocks traffic flow?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a collision.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a collision.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at collisions causes traffic jams and should be avoided.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Rely only on your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, put your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly out the rear window. Mirrors do not show everything behind your vehicle. Back up slowly.

questions.question: Motorcycle, scooter, and moped operators:

options.text: Are easy to see and are predictable.
Must share a traffic lane with another vehicle.
Have the right to use a complete traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have the right to use a complete traffic lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle, scooter, and moped riders share the road with you. Watch for them ahead so you have time to change lanes or slow down safely. Braking too suddenly can cause a crash.

questions.question: If the steering wheel is a clock face, where should your hands be?

options.text: 9 and 3 o'clock.
11 and 4 o'clock.
9 and 12 o'clock.

questions.correctAnswerText: 9 and 3 o'clock.
questions.explanation: Place your hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel (left hand at 8-10 o'clock and right hand at 2-4 o'clock). This position lets you turn the wheel without moving your hands on high-speed roads.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.
Pump the brakes rapidly.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, stay calm. Hold the steering wheel firmly and remove your foot from the gas pedal. Lightly apply the brakes when safe. Do not move to the shoulder until the car has slowed down.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink and drive.
Slippery when wet.
Road curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet.
